title: Claude Opus 5.5 （High） 以 1509 分登顶 Arena Text Arena 榜首
content:
Claude Opus 5.5（High）以 1509 分在 Text Arena 首次登顶第 1 名！
相比 Opus 5（High）提升了 18 分，后者目前位列第 11 名。Opus 4.6（High）仍稳居第 2 名，仅落后榜首 4 分。此次发布让 @AnthropicAI 包揽了 Text Arena 的前六名！
Opus 5.5（High）还以每百万 token 输入/输出定价计算的混合价格 $16/MToken 登上了 Text Arena 的帕累托前沿！其位置见下方帖子。
祝贺 @AnthropicAI 团队发布新模型！

report.summary: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (High) debut takes first place on Text Arena with 1509 points, lifting Anthropic to the top six spots.
report.background: Text Arena (the text arm of LMArena, formerly Chatbot Arena) ranks models by blind, crowd-sourced pairwise votes rather than vendor-run benchmarks, making it a widely cited proxy for real-world preference. Anthropic has steadily consolidated that leaderboard: Opus 4.6 (High) previously sat near the top, and Opus 5 (High) held a strong placement before slipping to 11th. The new Opus 5.5 (High) now scores 1509, an 18-point gain over Opus 5 and only 4 points ahead of Opus 4.6, which suggests the frontier is compressing into a narrow band of near-ties. Meanwhile, the "High" label signals an elevated reasoning-effort configuration, and the appearance of a $16 per million token blended price on the Pareto frontier reflects the industry's growing focus on capability-per-dollar, not raw scores alone.
key_points: Claude Opus 5.5 (High) scored 1509 on Text Arena, taking the No. 1 slot for the first time and beating its predecessor Opus 5 (High) by 18 points, which now sits at No. 11.
Anthropic now occupies all six top positions on Text Arena, a level of leaderboard concentration rarely seen and a signal of its current dominance in head-to-head human preference voting.
The gap at the top is tiny: Opus 4.6 (High) remains second, just 4 points behind the new flagship, implying the frontier models are effectively tied within noise for many users.

Beyond raw quality, Opus 5.5 (High) landed on Text Arena's Pareto frontier with a blended price of $16 per million tokens (input/output), meaning it is competitive on capability-per-dollar, not just capability.

The "High" reasoning setting matters for interpretation: results reflect a premium inference configuration, so cost, latency, and default-mode performance may differ from what a typical API user experiences.
report.impact: For the AI industry, a 1509-point leaderboard sweep reinforces Anthropic's position as the default quality benchmark, pressuring OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and open-weight challengers to answer on both score and price. The 18-point generational jump and 4-point gap to Opus 4.6 suggest rapid iteration with diminishing returns per release, which shifts competition toward cost, latency, context handling, and agentic reliability. For developers, a stronger, Pareto-efficient top model widens options but raises switching and evaluation costs, since "High" reasoning modes can be too slow or expensive for high-volume production. For regular users, the practical effect is better answers in assistant and coding products, though most gains will arrive indirectly through apps rather than the raw leaderboard. Expect price cuts and new mid-tier models as rivals respond.
report.tools: To follow the trend, watch LMArena (lmarena.ai) for live Text Arena rankings and Pareto frontier charts, and AI Analytics trackers such as Artificial Analysis for price-versus-quality comparisons. For independent replication, try the open-source FastChat / Chatbot Arena stack (GitHub: lm-sys/FastChat), LiveBench, and HELM for broader evaluation. Developers can compare Anthropic's model tiers via the Claude API docs and test cost trade-offs with prompt-evaluation tools like promptfoo or LangSmith.
